# PII / OCR masking (implemented for Jira MCP + curl access, generated .feature files, and Jira image attachments; general DOM/screenshot OCR still deferred)

**Status: partially implemented**, porting the same design already proven out on the Claude Code side of this project (see [.github/memory/decision-log.md](../memory/decision-log.md) once populated). Real detection and redaction code exists here and is wired into hook registrations for Jira tool calls (both the Atlassian-MCP-tool path and the terminal/`curl` path). Image attachments on a Jira story are also covered — but via an explicit agent-vision step inside `jira-story-readiness`, not a hook (see "Fourth consumer" below); general DOM/screenshot OCR outside that specific flow is still deferred.

## What's implemented
- [pii-scanner.js](pii-scanner.js) — deterministic, dependency-free regex detector for emails, phone numbers, SSN-like government IDs, payment card numbers, and common secret patterns (AWS/GitHub/generic API keys, bearer tokens, `password:`/`api_key:`-style assignments). Exposes `scanText()` and `redactText()`.
- [sanitize.js](sanitize.js) — the hook entrypoint. Reads the hook's stdin JSON, runs the scanner against `tool_input`/`tool_output`, and returns `updatedInput`/`updatedToolOutput` with matches replaced by `[REDACTED:<TYPE>-n]` placeholders. Writes the placeholder→original redaction map to `audit/pii-scan-results/` for authorized human lookup only — never echoed back to the model. Registered via [.github/hooks/jira-pretool-guard.json](../hooks/jira-pretool-guard.json) and [.github/hooks/jira-posttool-guard.json](../hooks/jira-posttool-guard.json), scoped to this environment's Atlassian MCP tool calls (verify the exact tool-name prefix empirically per environment).
- **PII entity scope, as implemented:** EMAIL, PHONE, SSN, CREDIT_CARD, and secret-shaped strings (API_KEY_AWS, API_KEY_GITHUB, API_KEY_GENERIC, BEARER_TOKEN, GENERIC_SECRET). Test data like names/emails/postal codes used in SauceDemo/CURA Healthcare test fixtures is public demo data, not real PII — see [copilot-instructions.md](../copilot-instructions.md)'s credentials rule for the equivalent public-demo-data carve-out; the scanner still flags an email-shaped string wherever it appears (it can't tell "public demo data" from "real"), so expect matches on legitimate test fixtures too — that's expected, not a bug.
- **PHONE matches unformatted numbers too.** Requiring a delimiter between digit groups (`987-654-3210`) missed real-world mobile numbers stored as a bare `9876543210` with no separators, so separators are optional — both formats match. Trade-off: any exact 10-digit unformatted number now matches, including some non-phone IDs that happen to be 10 digits long. The fixed-length pattern plus `\b` word boundaries at both ends still prevents it from matching a substring inside a longer digit run (a 12+ digit account/tracking number, a 16-digit card number) or an alphanumeric ID (no boundary between a letter and a digit) — see the rule's own comment in [pii-scanner.js](pii-scanner.js) for the detail. This affects every consumer of `scanText()` (both Jira hooks, the curl-path hook, the prompt-scan hook, and the `.feature`-file gate), not just one path.

## Second consumer: generated Playwright test files
[.github/scripts/scan-feature-for-pii.js](../scripts/scan-feature-for-pii.js) reuses `pii-scanner.js`'s `scanText()` for generated test artifacts before they are committed, not Jira tool I/O. The purpose is the same: block obvious credential/PII patterns from being introduced into local automation files. This consumer remains a defensive gate rather than a general-purpose scanner.

## Third consumer: curl-based Jira access
[.github/pii-ocr/sanitize.js](sanitize.js)'s `processBashJiraPayload()` extends the same `scanText()`/`redactText()` scanner to Jira access made via `curl` through this environment's terminal tool — the path [instructions/jira-access.instructions.md](../instructions/jira-access.instructions.md) actually directs use of for the one thing `jira-read.js` can't cover (binary attachment downloads), since it explicitly forbids the Atlassian MCP tool that `pretool-jira-guard.js`/`posttool-jira-guard.js` are scoped to. Without this, curl-based Jira responses have **zero** PII protection — the Atlassian-MCP-tool hooks never fire for them, and a terminal-tool `PostToolUse` hook with only token-truncation logic would have no PII logic at all.

Implementation notes, deliberately different from the other consumers:
- **Scoped by command text, not by tool name.** The terminal tool covers every shell command in the session, so scanning all of it would add cost and false-positive risk to unrelated commands (`git status`, `npm test`, ...). `isJiraCurlCommand()` only engages when `tool_input.command` references `JIRA_BASE_URL` or `atlassian.net` — everything else is a guaranteed no-op with no added work.
- Redaction runs inside the terminal tool's `PostToolUse` hook; any subsequent token-truncation passes operate on the already-redacted text.
- Writes to the same `audit/pii-scan-results/` directory, same redaction-map format, as the other consumers.

## Fifth consumer, and the canonical path going forward: `jira-read.js`
[.github/scripts/jira-read.js](../scripts/jira-read.js) is the **recommended path for any Jira issue/search text fetch**, ahead of both the Atlassian-MCP-tool hooks and the third consumer above:

- **Redacts in-process, before printing — no hook dependency at all.** It fetches via Node's own `fetch()` and calls `scanText()`/`redactText()` itself, in the same process, before writing anything to stdout. This sidesteps the "does the hook reliably fire" question entirely (see "Known potential gap" just below) rather than trying to work around it.
- **General-purpose, not skill-specific.** It's a CLI any skill/agent/prompt can call via the terminal tool, the same way `curl` was used — not logic baked into one skill's process.
- Writes to the same `audit/pii-scan-results/` directory, tagged `jira-read_<command>` (`jira-read_issue` / `jira-read_search`).
- **Does not replace the curl-path hook (third consumer, above) or the binary-download path (fourth consumer, below)** — it only covers `GET /issue` and `GET /search` text responses. Raw `curl` is still the only option for binary attachment downloads.

## Known potential gap: `curl -o file` / `> file` bypasses the curl-path hook entirely
The curl-path hook (above) only scans the terminal tool's own captured stdout/stderr. If a Jira curl call redirects its response body straight to disk (`-o <file>`, `--output <file>`, or shell `> file`) instead of printing to stdout, the hook sees nothing to scan — no error, no audit entry, just silent pass-through. The content only enters context later via a separate file-read, which has **no PII hook wired to it at all**.

**Mitigation chosen: docs-only, not a new hook.** Rather than adding file-read scanning (broad blast radius — every file read in every session, not just Jira fetches), [instructions/jira-access.instructions.md](../instructions/jira-access.instructions.md#never-redirect-a-text-response-curl-calls-output-to-a-file--let-it-print-to-stdout) explicitly forbids output-redirection on Jira curl text calls, reinforced directly in the `jira-story-readiness` skill and its backing agent. This is a policy fix, not a technical one — same category as the RBAC/tool-restriction model documented in [instructions/guardrails-policy.instructions.md](../instructions/guardrails-policy.instructions.md) (enforced by everyone respecting the stated rule, not by access control). If a future agent ignores the instruction and redirects anyway, nothing currently stops it.

## Fourth consumer: image attachment OCR via agent vision
`jira-story-readiness`'s process step for attachment handling (see its [SKILL.md](../skills/jira-story-readiness/SKILL.md)) closes part of the "images aren't covered at all" gap below — but differently from every other consumer here, and it's important not to conflate the two:

- **Not a hook. Cannot be a hook.** The other consumers are deterministic regex scripts that a hook system runs automatically, with no LLM involved. Reading text out of an arbitrary image requires vision — hooks are plain Node processes with no model access, so there is no way to make this run silently in the background the way the others do. It only happens when an agent explicitly does it as a step in its own turn.
- **The flow:** if the fetched issue's `attachment` field lists an image, the skill downloads it (`curl ... -o <file>` — a deliberate, narrow exception to the "never redirect" rule, since binary content can't meaningfully print to stdout; see [instructions/jira-access.instructions.md](../instructions/jira-access.instructions.md#exception-downloading-a-binary-attachment-eg-an-image-does-require--o-file)), reads it with the file-viewing tool, and the agent transcribes whatever text it sees. That transcription is piped into [.github/scripts/scan-ocr-text-for-pii.js](../scripts/scan-ocr-text-for-pii.js), which reuses the same `scanText()`/`redactText()` as everything else and writes to the same `audit/pii-scan-results/` directory — but tagged `hook_event_name: "SkillStep_ImageOCR"`, deliberately never `"PreToolUse"`/`"PostToolUse"`, so it's never mistaken for a real hook firing when someone's reading the audit log later.
- **Accuracy is not guaranteed.** Unlike regex matching (deterministic — same input always produces the same match), an LLM transcribing an image can misread, skip, or hallucinate text. Report findings from this path as best-effort, not as a verified scan, and say so explicitly — this matters if findings from this path are ever shown to a client or stakeholder as evidence.

## Still deferred
- **DOM/screenshot/OCR sanitization during general browser use** — a Playwright MCP snapshot taken for reasons unrelated to Jira attachments (e.g. testing a live app) still has no PII coverage at all; the fourth consumer above is scoped specifically to Jira image attachments inside `jira-story-readiness`, not a general Playwright MCP hook.
- Coverage beyond Jira (MCP path, curl path, and image attachments): TestRail responses, generic file reads.
- The curl path's `PreToolUse` side (the outbound command/request itself) is not scanned — only the response (`PostToolUse`). A curl command that embedded literal PII in a POST body (rather than referencing it via env var, which `copilot-instructions.md`'s credentials rule already requires) would not be caught before executing.
- There is no PII hook at all for non-image file reads (see the gap above) — this matters beyond Jira too, for any text file containing PII that gets read directly.
- A **real, deterministic OCR library** is still not wired in anywhere — the fourth consumer above relies on an LLM's own vision reading, which is a different (and less verifiable) mechanism than the regex scanning used everywhere else in this file.

## Relationship to existing rules
This is the concrete-tooling counterpart to the Data Protection controls described in [instructions/guardrails-policy.instructions.md](../instructions/guardrails-policy.instructions.md) and enforced by `copilot-instructions.md`'s "never hardcode real credentials or secrets" rule. The remaining deferrals and exclusions are intentionally described in the active governance docs rather than a dedicated Phase 1 summary file.

## Open verification items for this Copilot-native port
- Exact Atlassian MCP tool-name prefix (assumed `mcp_atlassian-mcp_*` based on this workspace's current environment) and exact terminal-tool name (assumed `run_in_terminal`) should be confirmed empirically once these hooks are live at a true workspace root — see the relevant scripts' own header comments in [.github/scripts/](../scripts/).
- Whether this environment's hook payload shape matches Claude Code's (`tool_response.{stdout,stderr}` for terminal calls, `tool_output` for MCP calls) is unconfirmed — the ported scripts keep the same shape assumptions with an explicit comment flagging this as unverified, per this project's known-risks list.
